items.title: 68163_Tom Whaley oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] These were Italian piano players. [INTERVIEWEE] No, he was a leader. He had three sons, and he knew music and he'd stand up there with his baton and when you'd make a bad note he'd hit your hand

ctx.x: And across the street from where I lived, there was an Italian. They had two sons, I know, and he was a teacher, see -- and he was teaching, and I'd go over his house, and sit down and play the piano and he had a
great big long baton, see, as long as this cane, and when I'd make a bad note, he'd hit my hands, so I told my mother, "I ain't going over there any more, the man hit my hand!'
